props.title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
props.initialSlug: A life in reverse, a love eternal.

sections.content: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button stands as David Fincher's most ambitious departure from his darker repertoire. Based on F. Scott Fitzgerald's short story, this reverse-aging epic shares DNA with Forrest Gump (1994) - both written by Eric Roth, both spanning decades of American history through an extraordinary protagonist. Fincher's meticulous visual effects pioneered new ground in aging/de-aging technology, paving the way for films like The Irishman (2019). Brad Pitt's subtle performance captures Benjamin's peculiar displacement - a man moving backwards through time while those around him march forward.

sections.content: The film's meditation on mortality aligns with other philosophical explorations of time and aging. Arrival (2016) similarly plays with non-linear storytelling to examine how we experience time and loss. Cloud Atlas (2012) weaves multiple timelines to show how souls might journey across centuries. What sets Benjamin Button apart is its intimate focus on relationships - particularly between Benjamin and Daisy, whose lives intersect at various points only to cross paths most perfectly when they're the same age. SUBHEAD: Visual Innovation and Period Detail

Fincher's attention to period authenticity rivals that of Once Upon a Time in America (1984) and The Godfather Part II (1974). Each era feels lived-in rather than costumed. The film's groundbreaking CGI work on Brad Pitt's various ages influenced later films like Gemini Man (2019) and Captain Marvel (2019). The New Orleans setting provides rich historical texture, from the 1918 flu pandemic to Hurricane Katrina, anchoring Benjamin's fantastic journey in real historical moments.
